_README: Upgrade-screen readings for the reference GR86. This is the SECOND car for
the parts group — the Civic's rows live in
THE UPGRADE SCREEN IS A CONTROLLED A/B. It shows every readout for the
installed part AND for the alternative, side by side, with no tune drift
between the two halves. Nothing has to be bought to read it. Five pages
cycle with Toggle; page 1 (the six star ratings) is the only one not worth
capturing, because those are rounded to one decimal and derived from the
real numbers, and the PI appears on page 2 anyway.
So far this file holds the BASELINE ROW only — the car as it stands, with
the upgraded front track width installed. The stock-width halves are what
screen: upgrade menu — part preview, pages 2 to 5

build._note: Same build as the gearing and balance fixtures for this car.

baseline._state: Upgraded Front Track Width INSTALLED — the car as it currently stands

thePreviewSHOWSTHEDEFAULTTUNE: AN OPEN QUESTION, CLOSED BY THIS BASELINE. When the Civic's upgrade-screen
readings came in, its Mechanical Balance matched neither the default-tune
reading nor the live one, so the fixture recorded that the preview is
'computed at some tune state of its own' and warned that only DELTAS were
usable.
The GR86 baseline settles it three ways at once:
readout            preview     tuning menu, default tune
Mech. Balance        0.50          0.50
Aero Balance         0.45          0.45
Aero Efficiency      0.750         0.75
Three for three, and the car's LIVE tune at the time was nothing like its
default. So the preview shows the game's DEFAULT TUNE for the previewed
configuration, not whatever is currently dialled in.
THE ONE LOOSE END, recorded rather than smoothed over: the Civic's preview
read 0.46 where its default-tune tuning-menu reading was 0.47. One printing
step, on one readout, on one car, against three exact matches here. Most
likely a rounding difference between two code paths, but it is not
explained and it is not being explained away.
WHY IT MATTERS: it means every upgrade-screen A/B is directly comparable to
a default-tune reading, so the parts group and the balance group share a
reference point rather than living in separate worlds. It also means the
screen can be read WITHOUT restoring the default tune first, which is the
step whose absence caused the SPREAD disaster.
twoCarsSideBySide: Both at A 700, both AWD, so the differences are the cars and the parts.
Nothing is concluded from this — two cars differing in tires, aero and
everything else is not an experiment. It is here because it is the first
time two complete, comparable rows have existed at all, and because two of
the differences are worth a second look later: the GR86 brakes 8 ft better
and corners harder on semi-slicks, and gives up 25 mph of top speed at a
much worse aero efficiency, which is what a downforce build looks like.
